subject: On-prem edge redirect causing partial flows — trace + remediation plan
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@bluepeak.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partial TCP flows after eBPF redirect enable (site: dca1)

Hi Sofia,

We're seeing intermittent application errors for traffic to our on-prem inference host behind the BluePeak edge (dca1). Symptoms: client uploads fail ~40% of the time with TCP resets mid-stream; wireshark shows payloads trimmed to ~1388-1404 bytes before RST. This started right after we enabled your new eBPF redirect chain last night.

What we observed so far:
- tcpdump on edge shows SYN/ACK exchange fine, then subsequent data packets get RSTs from the host side.
- DF bits set on some traceroutes showed MTU 1500 on path but we see large segments being fragmented elsewhere.
- conntrack shows many ESTABLISHED entries for the same 5-tuple appearing/disappearing rapidly.

Attached: capture-20280530.pcap.gz (trimmed), edge-conntrack-log-20280530.txt

Can your team take a look? We're preparing to roll-back the eBPF redirect but want to understand the root cause and a safe remediation plan.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Chen
Netops Lead, BluePeak Cloud

Subject: Fwd: Partial TCP flows after eBPF redirect enable (site: dca1)

Forwarding BluePeak's report — they have packet capture and conntrack logs attached. Quick notes from my initial triage:

- Reproduced symptom in staging when toggling the eBPF redirect: flows to the on-prem frontdoor sometimes get SNAT mapping churn.
- Evidence points to two simultaneous issues that amplify each other: MTU/clamping (packets being fragmented or dropped when DF=1) and aggressive conntrack timeouts/port reuse on our SNAT edge.
- Security groups on the private host only allow the canonical 30000-35000 ephemeral ports; BluePeak reports ephemeral flows outside that range during retries.

Immediate asks:
1) Jonas — can you review the conntrack excerpt and confirm whether we are seeing conntrack overload or erroneous SYN retry handling?
2) Marissa — can you draft a rollback checklist for BluePeak (how to safely disable eBPF redirect and revert iptables rules)?
3) I'll engage infra to test MTU clamping and a conservative ephemeral port expansion on a staging edge this afternoon.

I'll include steps and a proposed maintenance window once we have confirmation.

Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@bluepeak.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Partial TCP flows after eBPF redirect enable (site: dca1)

Sofia — quick read of edge-conntrack-log-20280530.txt (thanks Alice). Observations:

- High rate of conntrack DELETE for ESTABLISHED entries followed immediately by new SYNs on the same 5-tuple. That suggests the SNAT mapping is being dropped from the kernel conntrack table and the client sees a new 3-way handshake attempt. When that overlaps with application-level retries, you end up with half-open flows and RSTs.
- I also see packet-size clustering: lots of retransmissions with MSS ~1460 then a set of bursts around 1400 bytes before a reset. That looks like PMTU or middlebox fragmentation + the host or SG dropping fragments.

Possible causes to test (in order):
1) Conntrack table churn / low nf_conntrack max. Check /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max and nf_conntrack_buckets on the edge. If it's low, increase by 2x and monitor.
2) SNAT sticky entries timing out because of aggressive conntrack timeout tuning (tcp-timeout small). Compare conntrack timeouts on our edge image vs upstream kernel defaults.
3) Security group / firewall dropping fragmented packets (SGs that implicitly drop fragments are common). BluePeak should allow fragments or clamp MSS on the edge so hosts don't send large segments.
4) eBPF redirect path might be unintentionally modifying the DF bit or rewriting ip headers when offloading to XDP — verify header rewrite code paths.

Quick mitigation to suggest to BluePeak:
- Apply MSS clamp to 1340 on the edge redirect interface (this avoids fragments).
- Expand ephemeral port allowance on the host SG to 30000-61000 until we root-cause conntrack churn.
- Increase nf_conntrack_max to 1.5-2x current and monitor conntrack hits/drops.

If these mitigate, schedule a controlled test where we re-enable eBPF redirect with additional conntrack knobs and packet capture.

I'll paste a short commands checklist below they can run with minimal impact.

-- commands (run as root on the edge):
ip link set dev redir0 mtu 1500
ectl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=$(( $(cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max) * 2 ))
iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1340
# Expand ephemeral port SGs on destination host: allow tcp/udp 30000-61000 inbound from edge

Jonas
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@bluepeak.com>, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial TCP flows after eBPF redirect enable (site: dca1) — proposed maintenance and playbook

Alice — thanks for the capture and logs. Based on Jon's notes and my rollback checklist, here's a minimal-impact remediation playbook we can run in a coordinated 30-minute maintenance window. I've attached a short playbook (remediation-playbook.md) with exact commands and verification steps.

Planned actions (order matters):
1) Apply MSS clamp on BluePeak edge redirect (TCPMSS set-mss 1340) — immediate mitigation for fragmentation/RSTs. Verify by running repeated uploads to reproduce.
2) Expand host SG ephemeral port range to 30000-61000 (temporary) and monitor for port-reuse-related retries.
3) On edge: increase nf_conntrack_max and watch /proc/net/nf_conntrack counters; also capture conntrack hits/insert/drop before and after.
4) If the above stabilizes traffic, enable debug-level conntrack logging for 1 hour and schedule a follow-up to analyze churn.
5) Only if we still see issues, roll back eBPF redirect (steps in playbook) and run a controlled redeploy with conservative eBPF changes (disable header-rewrite branch).

Roll-back checklist highlights (for BluePeak):
- Stop redirectd service: systemctl stop redirectd
- Remove iptables rules created by redirect: iptables-save | grep redirectd and iptables -D as needed
- Confirm traffic flows directly to traditional SNAT path and re-run the capture for 10 minutes

Verification (post-change):
- Confirm sustained upload success rate > 99% across 1k test uploads
- Validate no excessive conntrack deletions in /proc/net/nf_conntrack
- Collect 5-minute pcap to ensure MSS/fragment behavior fixed

We propose the maintenance window: Fri 2028-05-31 22:00-22:30 UTC (low traffic for your app). If that's OK, we'll coordinate on a shared Slack channel and I will be on the call.

Attachments: remediation-playbook.md (contains step-by-step commands and roll-back steps)

Marissa
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
